controllingAuthority.summary: On a not-guilty verdict by judge or jury on all counts, the presiding judge must ask the acquitted person whether they want the records removed and destroyed, and if the answer is yes the court issues the order immediately with no separate petition. The section was renumbered by Public Chapter 268 of 2025, effective 2025-04-24: the acquittal ground that sat at former § 40-32-101(a) is now within § 40-32-106, whose non-conviction grounds include a verdict of not guilty, and which carries the acquittal-in-open-court procedure. No fee may be charged: § 40-32-106(a)(1) provides that qualifying public records must be removed and destroyed without cost to the person. Under § 40-32-110 expunction restores the person, in contemplation of law, to the status occupied before arrest, indictment, information, trial and conviction.

exclusions: A partial acquittal. The immediate route runs on a not-guilty verdict on all counts; a mixed-count case routes to the redaction analysis instead.
A person who was never asked at the verdict, or who declined at the time and later changed their mind. That person routes to the non-conviction petition track, which remains open.
This track offers no participant filing. The order issues in open court on the judge's own question.

waitingPeriods.duration: The not-guilty verdict itself. The order issues immediately in open court and there is no waiting period.
The court sends the order to the TBI within 30 days. Nothing changes on a background check until it arrives.

geography.venue: Not applicable. The order issues in the trial court in open court at the verdict; nothing is filed and there is no venue for a participant submission.

destination.name: The trial court, in open court at the verdict

components.notes: Explains what should have happened at the verdict — that the judge must ask and that the order issues immediately at no cost — so a participant who was asked knows what they were being offered; establishes whether the acquittal was on all counts, since a partial acquittal is a different analysis; helps the participant verify whether the order in fact issued and reached the TBI within 30 days; and routes to the non-conviction petition track where the judge did not ask, or where the person declined at the time and has since changed their mind.

controllingAuthority.summary: Created by Public Chapter 268 of 2025, effective 2025-04-24, and codified by Public Chapter 608 effective 2026-03-25. All public records of a person charged with a misdemeanour or felony must, upon petition by that person to the court having jurisdiction in the previous action, be removed and destroyed without cost to the person where the charge was dismissed other than by diversion completion, a no true bill was returned, the person was arrested and released without being charged, a nolle prosequi was entered, a verdict of not guilty was returned, or on the section's further grounds including qualifying implied-consent dismissals, abatement by death, mistaken identity and racial-justice-protest convictions. Subsection (a)(2) extends the same no-cost treatment to a successfully defended order of protection and to expired bonds under § 38-3-109. There is no waiting period. The TBI certificate under § 40-32-102(c) is not required for a § 40-32-106 expunction unless the expunction resulted from successful completion of pretrial or judicial diversion. Under § 40-32-110 expunction restores the person, in contemplation of law, to the status occupied before arrest, indictment, information, trial and conviction, and under § 40-32-102(e) the expunged records are confidential and unlawful release is a Class A misdemeanour.

exclusions: A dismissal that resulted from successful completion of a diversion programme, which routes to the pretrial or judicial diversion tracks and carries a clerk's fee rather than being free.
Any count in the case that resulted in a conviction. A mixed-count case routes to the redaction analysis.
Records in a county other than the one where the case originated, which require a separate filing in each county.

waitingPeriods.duration: None.

geography.venue: Statewide statute with originating-court venue. A person with cases in several counties files separately in each. There is no statewide participant form, so what varies locally is the clerk's own paperwork: the AOC directs filers to check with the court clerk because separate forms may be required for multiple charges.

components.notes: A controlled petition for expunction of public records drafted to T.C.A. § 40-32-106(a), identifying the court, the docket, the charge, the disposition and the ground relied on, stating the state control number from the TBI history, and requesting removal and destruction of all public records without cost. Tennessee publishes no participant expunction form: confirmed on 2026-08-06 by direct inspection of both AOC form indices. The statute supplies the court, the vehicle, the grounds and the relief, which is what makes a controlled pleading supportable.

States on the face of the packet that this route is free: § 40-32-106(a)(1) requires the records to be removed and destroyed without cost to the person. A participant asked for a fee on this route should query it with the clerk.

Explains where to file and that a separate filing is needed in each county; that expunction is not automatic and the record stays visible until the petition is filed; that no TBI certificate is required on this route unless the case came through diversion; and what happens after the order. A court ordering expunction shall send a copy of the order to the TBI within 30 days for entry into its expunged offender and pretrial diversion database. The order must contain the person's name, date of birth, social security number, the offence dismissed, the state control number referenced in § 8-4-115, the date and cause of dismissal, and the date the order was entered. Nothing changes on a background check until the order reaches the TBI, and the packet tells the participant to confirm that it did. Also explains the § 40-6-204(b) right the participant was supposed to be told about at charging.

controllingAuthority.summary: Public Chapter 268 of 2025 split the former § 40-32-101(g) conviction route along an eligibility and procedure seam: § 40-32-107 now defines who is an eligible petitioner and § 40-32-108 supplies the whole procedure. That mapping is officially corroborated rather than inferred — Public Chapter 268's own conforming amendments replaced the old citation to § 40-32-101(g)(3) with § 40-32-107 and the old § 40-32-101(g) with § 40-32-107(a)(1), and replaced procedural references to § 40-32-101 with § 40-32-108. Eligibility under § 40-32-107(a) turns on the offence being on one of the enumerated Class C, Class D or Class E felony lists or within the misdemeanour category subject to its exclusion list, the offence having occurred on or after 1 November 1989 and prior to any conviction for an expunction-ineligible offence including federal and out-of-state offences, no previous expunction under subsection (a), (b) or (c), and fulfilment of every sentence requirement including all fines, restitution, court costs and other assessments, completion of imprisonment or probation, all release conditions, and any required year free from dependency on or abuse of alcohol or a controlled substance. The waiting period at § 40-32-107(a)(3)(B) runs from completion of the sentence: five years for a misdemeanour or Class E felony and ten years for a Class C or Class D felony. Subsection (a)(4) directs the petitioner to § 40-32-108, whose subsection (e) requires the petition and proposed order to be prepared by the office of the district attorney general and given to the petitioner to file. Public Chapter 719, effective 2026-04-14, rewrote the § 40-32-108(d)(2) decision standard, preserving the rebuttable presumption for petitioners eligible under § 40-32-107(a)(1)(A) to (E) while directing the court to weigh the petitioner's interest against the best interests of justice and public safety. Public Chapter 930, effective 2026-07-01 and applying only to offences committed on or after that date, relocated burglary under § 39-13-1002 from the Class E list to the Class D list, which doubles the wait for that offence from five to ten years prospectively only.

geography.venue: Statewide statute with originating-court venue and prosecutor-office routing. The request goes to the office of the district attorney general for the judicial district of the convicting court, because § 40-32-108(e) makes that office the preparer of the petition. destination.detail: Section 40-32-108(e) requires the petition and proposed order to be prepared by the district attorney general's office and given to the petitioner to be filed with the clerk. Both the Tennessee AOC and the TBI direct participants to request a conviction expungement packet from that office. LegalEase generates the participant's request and eligibility record; it does not generate the petition or the order, because those are prosecutor and court instruments.

components.notes: A controlled written request to the office of the district attorney general asking it to prepare the petition and proposed order under T.C.A. § 40-32-108(e). It identifies the convicting court and docket, the offence and its exact statutory section, the date of the offence and of the conviction, the date the sentence was completed, and the statutory basis for eligibility, and it asks for the conviction expungement packet the AOC and TBI both direct participants to request.

A supporting record assembled from the participant's answers and their own documents: the offence mapped to its exact T.C.A. section, the waiting-period computation from completion of the sentence, proof that all fines, restitution, court costs and other assessments are paid, confirmation that any imprisonment or probation is complete and all release conditions met, and the no-other-conviction position from the TBI history. This is what the district attorney's office needs to prepare the petition and what the court reviews under § 40-32-108(d).

Explains the whole chain and who controls each link: the participant requests the packet from the district attorney general; that office prepares the petition and proposed order and gives them to the participant; the participant files with the clerk and pays the clerk's fee under § 8-21-401; the clerk serves the district attorney, who may submit recommendations within 60 days and may file evidence under seal; the court may not order sooner than 61 days after service, must review the TBI certificate required by § 40-32-102(c), and weighs the interest of the petitioner against the best interests of justice and public safety with a rebuttable presumption in favour of a petitioner eligible under § 40-32-107(a)(1)(A) to (E); and on denial no further petition may be filed for two years. Under T.C.A. § 40-32-102(c)(1) the TBI develops a request-for-certification form that is completed by the court and submitted to the TBI before an order of expunction is entered, and under (c)(3) an order must not be entered unless the certificate is attached to it. The TBI determines whether the offence is eligible under § 40-32-107 or § 40-32-105 and notes the determination on the certificate; under (c)(4) the certificate certifies offence eligibility only, not defendant eligibility, and the court retains the duty to determine eligibility. The court is exempt from the certificate requirement for expunctions under § 40-32-109 and § 40-32-106 unless the expunction follows successful completion of pretrial diversion under §§ 40-15-102 to 40-15-107 or judicial diversion under § 40-35-313. This is a court instrument completed by court staff. LegalEase does not generate it, does not complete it and does not assert it has been obtained. A court ordering expunction shall send a copy of the order to the TBI within 30 days for entry into its expunged offender and pretrial diversion database. The order must contain the person's name, date of birth, social security number, the offence dismissed, the state control number referenced in § 8-4-115, the date and cause of dismissal, and the date the order was entered. Nothing changes on a background check until the order reaches the TBI, and the packet tells the participant to confirm that it did.

controllingAuthority.summary: Read at source on 2026-08-06. Section 40-32-107(b) defines an eligible petitioner as a person seeking expunction of no more than two offences. Each offence must be eligible under § 40-32-107(a)(1) and must have occurred prior to any conviction for an expunction-ineligible offence, including ineligible federal and other-state convictions. The permitted combinations are exhaustive: two misdemeanours, or one felony and one misdemeanour. Two felonies are not available on this route. At filing there must be five years since completion of sentence for any misdemeanour or Class E felony being expunged and ten years for any Class C or Class D felony being expunged, every sentence requirement must be fulfilled for each offence, and the person must not previously have been granted expunction under subsection (a), this subsection (b) or subsection (c). Subsection (b)(2) provides a single-episode merger mirroring (a)(1)(F): contemporaneous same-location single-intent convictions count as a single offence for the purposes of the two-offence limit, so one episode does not consume both slots. Subsection (b)(3) directs the petitioner to § 40-32-108, so the same DA-prepared petition procedure applies. The reciprocal bars across (a), (b) and (c) are lifetime, which is why using this pathway forecloses a later second use and makes the timing decision consequential.

destination.detail: Section 40-32-108(e) requires the petition and proposed order to be prepared by the district attorney general's office and given to the petitioner to be filed with the clerk. Both the Tennessee AOC and the TBI direct participants to request a conviction expungement packet from that office. LegalEase generates the participant's request and eligibility record; it does not generate the petition or the order, because those are prosecutor and court instruments.

components.notes: A controlled written request to the office of the district attorney general asking it to prepare the petition and proposed order under T.C.A. § 40-32-108(e). It identifies the convicting court and docket, the offence and its exact statutory section, the date of the offence and of the conviction, the date the sentence was completed, and the statutory basis for eligibility, and it asks for the conviction expungement packet the AOC and TBI both direct participants to request.

A supporting record assembled from the participant's answers and their own documents: the offence mapped to its exact T.C.A. section, the waiting-period computation from completion of the sentence, proof that all fines, restitution, court costs and other assessments are paid, confirmation that any imprisonment or probation is complete and all release conditions met, and the no-other-conviction position from the TBI history. This is what the district attorney's office needs to prepare the petition and what the court reviews under § 40-32-108(d).

Explains the whole chain and who controls each link: the participant requests the packet from the district attorney general; that office prepares the petition and proposed order and gives them to the participant; the participant files with the clerk and pays the clerk's fee under § 8-21-401; the clerk serves the district attorney, who may submit recommendations within 60 days and may file evidence under seal; the court may not order sooner than 61 days after service, must review the TBI certificate required by § 40-32-102(c), and weighs the interest of the petitioner against the best interests of justice and public safety with a rebuttable presumption in favour of a petitioner eligible under § 40-32-107(a)(1)(A) to (E); and on denial no further petition may be filed for two years. Under T.C.A. § 40-32-102(c)(1) the TBI develops a request-for-certification form that is completed by the court and submitted to the TBI before an order of expunction is entered, and under (c)(3) an order must not be entered unless the certificate is attached to it. The TBI determines whether the offence is eligible under § 40-32-107 or § 40-32-105 and notes the determination on the certificate; under (c)(4) the certificate certifies offence eligibility only, not defendant eligibility, and the court retains the duty to determine eligibility. The court is exempt from the certificate requirement for expunctions under § 40-32-109 and § 40-32-106 unless the expunction follows successful completion of pretrial diversion under §§ 40-15-102 to 40-15-107 or judicial diversion under § 40-35-313. This is a court instrument completed by court staff. LegalEase does not generate it, does not complete it and does not assert it has been obtained. A court ordering expunction shall send a copy of the order to the TBI within 30 days for entry into its expunged offender and pretrial diversion database. The order must contain the person's name, date of birth, social security number, the offence dismissed, the state control number referenced in § 8-4-115, the date and cause of dismissal, and the date the order was entered. Nothing changes on a background check until the order reaches the TBI, and the packet tells the participant to confirm that it did.

participantInputs.question: Which court handled the case, and in which county? A separate filing is needed in each county where you have a case.
What is the docket or case number?
What was the charge, and exactly how did the case end?
On what date did the case end?
What is the state control number on your TBI criminal history? The expunction order cannot be completed without it.
List every other conviction you have anywhere, including federal and out-of-state.
Are you asking about this because of immigration, federal employment or a security clearance? Tennessee expunction does not reach federal records.
What is the exact T.C.A. section you were convicted under? The offence name and class are not enough — Tennessee's eligible lists are section by section.
On what date was the offence committed? This matters independently of the conviction date, because a 2026 change applies only to offences committed on or after 1 July 2026.
Did the conviction occur on or after 1 November 1989?
On what date did you finish the entire sentence — including any imprisonment or probation, all release conditions, and every fine, restitution amount, court cost and other assessment?
Is every fine, restitution amount, court cost and other assessment paid in full? Anything outstanding means the sentence is not complete and the clock has not started.
Have you ever had a conviction expunged in Tennessee before? This route is available once in a lifetime and a previous grant closes it.
Did you hold a commercial driver licence at the time, and did the offence involve a controlled substance or a commercial motor vehicle?
Did your sentence require a period free from dependency on or abuse of alcohol or a controlled substance? If so, have you met at least one year of it?
How many offences are you asking to clear? The limit is two.
Are the two offences both misdemeanours, or one felony and one misdemeanour? Two felonies cannot be done on this route.
Did the offences happen at the same time and place as part of one continuous incident with a single intent? If so they may count as one, leaving your second slot open.
This pathway can be used once in your life. Do you have any other conviction that might become eligible later? Using it now closes the door on that.

legalDesignDecision.rationale: Process guidance is retained on two substantive grounds and on an adopted exclusion, not on the absence of a form or of text. The adopted readiness record marks this mechanism as outside the current self-help scope, which is an exact product-scope exclusion a normalization worker preserves rather than reopens. Independently, both guidance rationales are in the preserved group and both are real here: establishing that an offence was committed as a consequence of being trafficked is a contested evidentiary showing, and presenting it is individualized advocacy in a survivor-sensitive setting. The node is deliberately not deferred, because detect-name-refer does not depend on the unretrievable text: LegalEase can tell a participant that the route exists, where it sits, and who to go to, without stating a single eligibility condition. What is withheld is any description of the mechanism, and that is carried as a release blocker on the governing mechanism rather than a build blocker, because nothing is being built. The section's operative status rests on official cross-references in the enacted text of Public Chapter 268 rather than on the secondary profile the controlling review relied on, which is a source upgrade recorded here.
